title: Water, Tea, Milk, and Bread
label: ch:pa-request-food-drink
canDo: I can politely ask for water, tea, milk, or bread in Punjabi, name which of the four is a loanword and which is inherited with an unknown root, and hear the difference between a tone that stays level and one that never formed at all.

payoff.summary: The chapter closes on ਰੋਟੀ, the request that breaks the drink pattern: the reader produces all four requests with ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ, sorts ਪਾਣੀ and ਦੁੱਧ (inherited, known root) against ਚਾਹ (loaned from Chinese by the overland route, carrying Punjabi's first noun-level tone) against ਰੋਟੀ (inherited, root unknown), and names the first Punjabi chapter to realize polite requesting at all.
